task: degeneracy: is the SFT loop a greedy-decoding artifact? code-500 on sft_p324_v2 at t=0.8
why: SFT raised degenerate repetition from base 0-shot 24.7% to 55.8% (8-gram x3+, n=500, delta=6.3%). The model emits English markdown boilerplate on Chinese coding questions and loops before reaching code; the 12.2% fence rate and 2.2% accuracy are downstream of that.
reading: degeneracy at t=0.8 below base's 24.7% => the loop is a decoding artifact and every greedy code-500 number today measures the decoder, not the model. At or above 55.8% => the model is non-terminating and the cause is upstream. Accuracy at t=0.8 is a different estimator and is NOT comparable to the greedy 2.2%.

task: SFT pack truncation: what fraction of answer spans hit the 4096 boundary without an <eos>?
why: A truncated answer literally supervises 'do not stop'. Highest-prior cause of the 55.8% degeneracy, and code answers are longer than math ones so it would also explain why code degrades more.
reading: truncation >=10% and higher on code rows => data is the cause; the fix is length filtering or chunking at pack time, not SFT hyperparameters. ~0% => data is not the cause, hand it to the decoding and hyperparameter arms.

task: SFT pack termination determinacy: cluster near-duplicate instructions, count distinct answer shapes per cluster
why: AGENTS.md's own rule -- multiple answer formats on identical prompts leave termination underdetermined -- was written for FoNE number formats and has never been checked on the code/math SFT corpus.
reading: a high share of clusters with >1 shape => termination is underdetermined by the data; the fix is normalising each cluster to one shape at pack time. Near zero => rule this cause out.

task: loader: tool turn rendering + loss mask on tool spans, enforced in test_sft_pack.py
why: The <<expr=result>> form teaches 'write the expression then the result' -- one continuous generation. An agent loop needs 'write the call then STOP', with the result given. Opposite behaviours on identical content; the single-span form trains a model that fabricates its own tool outputs.
reading: the tool turn costs 8 tokens and round-trips losslessly in the frozen vocabulary (verified 2026-08-31), so no new special token is needed. The constraint lands in test_sft_pack.py, not in a doc: every token between <|im_start|>tool and its <|im_end|> must carry label -100. Ship a failing case that proves the assertion fires.

task: context length: per-position loss curve within 4096 and behaviour beyond it, on ckpt_p324
why: NoPE means there is no RoPE to extrapolate; the 3 gated-MLA layers are full causal and the 9 KDA layers carry a fixed-size state, so the two halves may behave oppositely past the training length. Nobody has measured it, and an agent loop is the first thing that will hit it.
reading: smooth rise past 4096 => usable but degrading, fixable by training length. Cliff at 4096 => a hard bound, and the agent loop must close inside it -- a design constraint on 30B. Also: if loss rises within 4096, the usable context is shorter than the nominal one and THAT is the number that matters.

task: token cost of one agent loop under OUR frozen tokenizer, p50/p90/p99, code and math separately
why: Our vocabulary is ~1.7 chars/token on Chinese against nanochat's 4.8, so borrowed '4096 is enough' claims do not transfer -- comparing token counts across tokenizers is the cross-denominator error we already made three times today.
reading: p90 loop fits >=3 rounds in 4096 => 4096 stands. <2 rounds => 4096 is a hard constraint on the agentic goal: either lengthen it (which changes the frozen recipe and the comparability of every ladder point) or bound loop depth by design. Until this number exists, 'agentic' is a word in the 30B table.
